questions.q: Why are means of transport and communication called the lifelines of a nation's economy?
answer: Transport and communication are called lifelines because, like blood vessels, they keep the economy alive and moving.

answer.text: Goods and raw materials must move from farms, mines and factories to markets and consumers. Efficient roads, railways, pipelines, waterways and airways carry this trade quickly and cheaply, tying together production, distribution and consumption.
Transport connects distant regions, helps people travel for work, tourism and pilgrimage, and binds the country into a single unit, aiding administration and defence.
Post, telephone, internet and mass media spread information, support business and keep society connected.

answer: Because the whole economy depends on them, these networks are rightly called its lifelines.

questions.q: Compare the advantages of roadways and railways as means of transport in India.
answer: Roadways and railways are the two main land transport systems in India, each with its own strengths.

answer.text: Roads are cheaper to build than railways, can be laid over hilly, uneven and dissected land, and negotiate high gradients. They provide door-to-door service, so the cost of loading and unloading is lower, and they act as feeders to railways.

Railways are the principal mode for carrying heavy goods and large numbers of passengers over long distances at low cost. They make long journeys easier, promote trade, tourism and pilgrimage, and helped knit the country together since the first line ran in 1853.

answer: Thus roads suit short and difficult routes, while railways are ideal for long-distance bulk movement.

questions.q: How has international trade become an economic barometer of a country's prosperity?

answer.text: is the exchange of goods and services between countries, and it reflects a nation's economic health.

list: Exports earn foreign exchange and reflect the country's productive strength
Imports supply what the country lacks — machinery, oil and technology
A favourable balance of trade, where exports exceed imports, signals a healthy economy
The variety and value of what a country trades reveal the level and diversity of its development
